title: Sequence-chunk latency decomposer and cache-adjuster instrumentation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add a lightweight instrumentation layer that decomposes end-to-end completion latency into per-sequence-chunk contributions and attributes delta to KV cache interactions, prefetch behavior, and kernel execution. The goal is to produce actionable metrics and traces that answer: (1) which sequence regions cause most latency, (2) how many ms are attributable to cache miss vs kernel vs prefetch overhead, and (3) how these attributions impact per-token cost calculations. This ticket covers design, tracing hooks, sampling strategy, metrics format, log/trace pipeline updates, and dashboard wireframes.
background: We currently report request-level P95/P99 and coarse per-token averages. Operators and perf engineers need finer fidelity across long sequences where performance and cost are non-uniform (e.g., warm prefix + cold tail, long-form generation). Existing traces show kernel spans but lack a structured decomposition per sequence chunk and do not correlate easily with KV cache hits/misses or speculative prefetch attempts. This makes it hard to tune prefetch heuristics and kv cache policies for real workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation emits per-sequence-chunk timing spans (chunk boundaries configurable by token stride) with labels: chunk_index, chunk_length, cache_hit_ratio, prefetch_attempted
Metrics exported to metrics pipeline: chunk_latency_ms, kernel_ms, prefetch_ms, kv_miss_count, kv_hit_count, sample_weight
Traces include a lightweight tracecontext correlation ID and link to request-level trace for sampling-based reconstruction
Dashboards with: chunk-latency heatmap, cumulative cache-impact waterfall, and per-model cost-reconciliation view
End-to-end overhead of instrumentation < 0.8% p50 and <1.5% p99 for typical generation workloads (measured in synthetic harness)
Documentation and runbook describing how to interpret attribution and how to adjust prefetch and batching configs
steps: Design: finalize chunking strategy (fixed stride vs adaptive per-token-complexity) and sampling policy (1% full traces + 10% chunk-level metrics)
Implement trace hooks in runtime: emit chunk spans around emission loop with micro-timings for kernel, prefetch, and kv resolve
Add KV cache probes: counter for hit/miss per chunk and duration of KV lookup
Wire chunk metrics into metric exporter (prometheus/grafana pipeline and ingestion schema) and add tags for model, deployment, and config
Create log to trace mapping: ensure logs include trace_id and chunk_index for downstream correlation
Build dashboard panels (prototype in Grafana): heatmap, waterfall, and per-model rollup
Run synthetic benchmark across 3 model families and document overhead and signal quality
Ship alpha with feature flag and default disabled in production until rollout completes
decisions: Chunking default: fixed stride=64 tokens with opt-in adaptive mode; rationale: predictable aggregation and low implementation complexity
Sampling: 1% full-trace sampling to avoid trace storage blowup; 10% chunk metrics emitted with weighted sample counts to reconstruct overall distribution
Metric names will use 'seq_chunk_*' prefix to avoid collision with existing token_* metrics
Instrumentation will be implemented as non-blocking probes to avoid interfering with hot path; any blocking calls must be offloaded to an async aggregator
